newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's energy imports cost $1.2 billion in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's energy imports cost $1.2 billion in 1996.

text.p: Morocco's energy imports including crude oil rose 12.3 percent to 11.2 billion dirhams ($1.2 billion) in 1996, a state-run regulatory body said.
In its monthly newsletter received on Tuesday, the Office des Changes said "energy imports, including crude oil, rose to 11.288 billion dirhams in 1996, up from 10.053 billion dirhams in 1995".

It said the value of crude oil imports rose to 7.4 billion dirhams in 1996 from 6.7 billion in 1995, while the volume dropped to 9.9 million tonnes in 1996 from 10.3 million -- reflecting the rise in crude prices on the international market.
Coal imports, increasingly used in power stations in recent years, rose to 2.8 million tonnes worth 1.2 billion dirhams in 1996 from 1.9 million tonnes costing 816 million dirhams.
Other hydrocarbon products such as gas oil account for the rest of the energy imports.
Morocco, which has no oil of its own, imports most of its crude from Gulf countries including Iran for refining at its two refineries Samir and Societe Cherifienne des Petroles.
The authorities sold off state stakes in both plants to the Swedish-based Saudi Corral Petroleum Holding AB for $419 million last month, the privatisation ministry said.
Samir has a capacity of 6.25 million tonnes per year, or 80 percent of Morocco's refined oil products needs. SCP refinery handles the remaining 20 percent.
